behavior_constraints: Add a `diff` subcommand accepting `--old <path>` and `--new <path>`, both required
Validate both specs through the existing validation path with the same error codes as plan/list/hash
Exit 0 with exactly empty stdout (0 bytes) when the two specs' hash canonical forms are byte-identical

Exit 1 when specs differ, printing one or more newline-terminated lines in fixed order: added jobs (`+ <name>`), removed jobs (`- <name>`), then changed jobs (`~ <name> <field>: <old_repr> -> <new_repr>`)
Added jobs listed in walk order of the new spec; removed jobs in walk order of the old spec; changed jobs in walk order of the new spec
For changed jobs, emit only differing fields, in fixed order: workdir, command, deps, env, level
Field representations: workdir/command verbatim; deps as `[d1,d2,...]` in spec order, empty `[]`; env as `{k=v,...}` byte-sorted, empty `{}`; level as decimal
Walk order is the same level-major-then-byte-wise order used by list/hash; levels computed independently per spec
Exit 2 on flag/positional errors or validation errors, with exactly one `error: ...\n` line on stderr and empty stdout
On validation failure, prepend `old: ` or `new: ` to the error payload; report `old` first if both invalid
entities.summary: This round adds a read-only `diff` subcommand that validates two specs, compares their canonical forms, and prints a deterministic line-oriented diff of added/removed/changed jobs with exit codes 0/1/2.

instruction_head:
# jobforge diff

Add a new subcommand `diff` that compares two job specs and reports the
user-observable changes.

All existing behavior is unchanged.

## New subcommand: `jobforge diff --old <path> --new <path>`

Validates both specs with the existing validation path (same error
codes as `plan`/`list`/`hash`). On success, prints a deterministic
line-oriented diff of the two specs to stdout and exits with:

- `0` if the two specs are equivalent (no lines printed, exactly 0
  bytes on stdout)
- `
